claude_analysis.tam_assessment: Consumer and research EEG headset buyers are a niche market: Google Trends interest for 'EEG headset' averages 53 and is trending down, and the incumbents found are headset vendors (Emotiv, Zeto) and existing comparison guides (iMotions, ApparatusRanker), not a mass consumer audience.
claude_analysis.pricing_assessment: The extracted $1-$25 'prices' look like text fragments rather than real price points, and a comparison site would mostly earn one-time affiliate commissions of roughly $10 per headset sale, well below the $200 acquisition floor.
claude_analysis.legal_reasoning: The regulatory probe found no restriction signals (0 restriction hits, 0 government sources), so nothing limits who may publish headset comparisons.
key_risks: Established free comparison content (iMotions' 15+ device guide, a Frontiers systematic review, ApparatusRanker) already covers the query
Vendors own 40% of buyer-intent search results, so paid acquisition may be the only channel and costs more than a customer is worth
Search interest is trending down and sales are one-time, so there is no recurring revenue
key_opportunities: Search volume is still strong (average interest 53)
Active hobbyist communities such as r/BCI and OpenBCI users want help choosing hardware
Research and clinical buyers (Emotiv Epoc X, Zeto) spend enough that a B2B lead-generation model could earn more per referral
claude_analysis.value_reasoning: About 100000 potential buyers × about $10 affiliate revenue per buyer per year ≈ $1M total addressable annual revenue.
claude_analysis.probability_reasoning: The value per customer is below the acquisition floor with 7 price observations, which caps the probability at 0.01, and the crowded field of existing guides points to penetration under 1%.
